messages:
maria: Hey team — hit a nasty repro with the JS SDK when bundling for the Edge runtime using Vite. Works fine in Node, but runtime throws: "ReferenceError: require is not defined" (stack points into our CJS entry).

alex: Ugh. Can you share steps to reproduce? Vite config + package.json exports?

maria: Yep. Minimal steps below. Note this is an ESM app (type: "module") targeting edge (Cloudflare-like).

Commands:
```
npm init -y && npm i vite react react-dom
npm i ../packages/redwood-inference-js --save
# run dev: vite
```

package.json in the SDK (important bits):
```
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference-js",
  "version": "0.5.2-canary",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
    }
  },
  "main": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "module": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

app code: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'`

Runtime error (browser/edge):
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined
  at /@fs/…/node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs:1:21
  at __require (…)
```

jon: That smells like Vite/Esbuild resolving the package to the CJS entry even though the app is ESM. Maybe because some bundler step falls back to `main`? Vite sometimes uses `optimizeDeps`/esbuild commonjs detection.

sam: If Vite prebundles with esbuild it will load CJS for optimization unless you pin the ESM file. Two workarounds: add `optimizeDeps.include: ['@redwood/inference-js']` or alias `@redwood/inference-js` -> `@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.mjs` in `vite.config.ts`.

maria: Tried both — alias works for dev, but breaks sourcemaps and types in IDE because TS picks up `types` from package exports which still point to compiled `.d.ts` but source map mappings get funky. Also `optimizeDeps` fix doesn't help when we build for edge (ssr build) — rollup picks CJS at bundle-time in some cases.

alex: Could we change packaging to make ESM the primary entry (module first) and avoid `main` pointing at CJS? Or add a top-level `exports` condition for `node` vs `browser` vs `edge`?

maria: I tried flipping `main` and `module` but some consumers (older bundlers / rollup configs) still prefer `main`. We could add: `exports: { "./package.json": ... , "./*": ... }` but messy.

nat: Another option — ship a tiny proxy `entry.mjs` at package root that re-exports from `./dist/index.mjs` and add a `browser` field in package.json pointing to it. That often forces ESM in bundlers that respect `browser`.

jon: Also worth auditing our build output: is `dist/index.mjs` truly ESM (no `exports.` calls that transpile to require)? Sometimes our bundler runtime shim injects `require()` for interop. Check rollup plugin config for `commonjs()` and `interop` options.

maria: Good call — found this in our build: `output: { format: 'es', interop: 'auto' }` which can insert CJS interop wrappers if there are mixed imports. Rebuilding with `interop: false` produces cleaner ESM but tests failed in Node 12 so we reverted.

sam: For the short term, can we publish a canary that exposes a dedicated `dist/edge.mjs` and a package.json `exports` condition like: `"edge": "./dist/edge.mjs"`? Then Vite/Astro/Cloudflare that respect `exports` priority might pick it.

maria: I pushed a tiny canary: `0.5.3-edge.0` with `exports` including an `edge` condition. Still testing.

deploy-bot: Published @redwood/inference-js@0.5.3-edge.0 to npm (dist-tag: canary-edge).

maria: Quick results: Vite dev + edge target now loads the mjs entry, runtime error gone. BUT types in TS language server still try to resolve `./dist/index.cjs` for some reason when the monorepo has hoisted packages. VSCode shows mismatched types source mapping.

alex: Can you paste the tsserver lookup trace? Sometimes the language server uses `main` or `types` fields differently when `type: module` set at workspace root.

maria: Logged trace: it resolves `@redwood/inference-js` -> package.json -> uses `types` -> `./dist/index.d.ts` -> but the emitted `.d.ts` references `require()` in one path (from our build pipeline). Stack: `node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.d.ts: exported const createClient: (opts: any) => any; // types are generic`

jon: Sounds like our .d.ts generation strip/transform step produced CJS-shaped declarations. We should audit `tsconfig` `module` / `declaration` settings for the build. Maybe `declarationMap` will help with editor resolution.

sam: For reproducer, can we get a minimal repo (single file) that demonstrates both: 1) edge runtime require error and 2) TS types mapping to wrong file? If so, we can open a small PR to switch packaging and add CI smoke test that bundles with Vite/Esbuild and with Rollup SSR.

maria: I'll create a small repro repo and drop a link later. For now, steps to trigger both locally are above. Leaving notes: don't rely on `main` fallback; ensure `exports` explicit conditions; keep `module` as top-level and ensure `.mjs` artifacts are pure ESM (no interop wrappers).

nat: I can pair with you tomorrow to finalize the packaging change and add a Vite-based smoke test to the SDK repo.

maria: Thanks — will DM repro link and test matrix. Also adding: please upvote if you've seen similar issues in other SDK packages (:thumbsup:).

alex: Thanks for the detailed repro, saved us a lot of churn.

maria: TL;DR: Vite/esbuild prebundle + package exports + interop wrappers => CJS fallback in edge -> runtime require error. Workarounds: alias to mjs, optimizeDeps include, or publish explicit `edge`/`browser` ESM entry. Long-term fix: adjust packaging build to guarantee pure ESM entry and correct .d.ts mapping.
